item.title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79817-7

Using one Earth system model with increasingly complex plankton food webs, the study finds that greater ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven declines in ocean carbon export, suggesting simple models may underestimate future weakening.
item.dc:title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump

item.title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79750-9

Tabernanthe iboga produces the medically important alkaloids voacangine and ibogaine, but key steps in their biosynthesis, as well as the biosynthetic route to the structurally distinct alkaloid ibophyllidine, have remained unresolved. Using genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and biochemical reconstitution, the authors identify the missing enzymes required for coronaridine and voacangine biosynthesis, elucidate the complete pathway to ibophyllidine, and achieve heterologous production of voacangine in Nicotiana benthamiana.
item.dc:title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids

item.title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79649-5

Post-polymerization modification provides a route to upcycle polyolefin waste, but most current systems have long reaction times and are substrate specific. Here, the authors report the rapid C-H nitration of various polyolefins with high selectivity and functionalisation degrees, forming functionalised polyolefins with enhanced tensile and adhesive properties.
item.dc:title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79418-4

In this study, the authors used measurement data combined with modeling and machine learning to estimate global human generation of five individual ARGs and intI1, discharge, and surface-water abundance, highlighting hotspots of per-capita generation and total abundance.

item.title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78986-9

This study shows that arteriviruses, like coronaviruses, form pore complexes that span their double-membrane replication organelles, pointing to a conserved nidovirus strategy that links the synthesis, export and packaging of viral RNA.
item.dc:title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles

item.title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79489-3

In mass spectrometry imaging, smaller pixel sizes usually come at the cost of reduced signal and more complex sample preparation. Here, authors develop a gentle infrared laser ablation approach that maps metabolites and lipids at few-micron pixel sizes in fresh-frozen and clinical tissue in open air.
item.dc:title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels

item.title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79609-z

CD4 T cells are central to the pathogenesis of uveitis and related inflammatory responses by promoting myeloid cell infiltration. Here, by leveraging scRNA-seq and a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis, the authors identify the kinase Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 T cell differentiation, migration and metabolic reprogramming and as a coordinator of T cell-bone marrow crosstalk that contributes to myeloid-biased hematopoiesis.
item.dc:title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease

item.title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79576-5

item.title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79477-7

During the Medieval Warm Period, natural warming drove tropical cyclones poleward in the western North Pacific but equatorward in the North Atlantic. In the modern warm period, both basins shift poleward, likely due to anthropogenic warming.
item.dc:title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period

item.title: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
item.description:
Ankit Gupta, Mustafa Khammash
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79229-7
Abstract Stochastic reaction networks govern noise-driven dynamics in systems ranging from gene regulation to cellular signalling and population processes. Yet their high dimensionality and sensitivity to initial states obscure transient mechanisms and limit reliable inference from experimental data. Here, we show that stochastic reaction networks in biological systems often exhibit dominant low-dimensional spectral structure that shapes their dynamics. We develop a spectral framework based on the stochastic Koopman operator that identifies these dominant dynamical modes directly from simulated trajectories, yielding reduced representations with computable error bounds. This reduction enables accurate analytical descriptions of the time evolution of moments, parameter sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, while achieving order-of-magnitude computational gains relative to standard simulation-based methods. Applied to synthetic gene circuits, our framework reveals the spectral organisation of stochastic oscillators, enables systematic comparison of competing intracellular controllers, and facilitates inference of initial-state distributions from single-cell snapshot population data collected over time. Together, these results establish a principled spectral description of stochastic reaction dynamics and provide a foundation for analysing and inferring high-dimensional noise-driven biological systems.

item.title: Orbital spectroscopy links dust source composition to atmospheric acidity and nitrate
item.description:
Rubén Soussé Villa, Oriol Jorba, María Gonçalves Ageitos, Jeronimo Escribano, Vincenzo Obiso, Ron L. Miller, Longlei Li, Natalie M. Mahowald, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79201-5
Abstract Mineral dust affects atmospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate, yet its impacts remain uncertain because its mineral composition is poorly constrained. Here we combine NASA EMIT orbital imaging spectroscopy with a satellite-constrained global chemistry model to quantify how source-resolved calcite variability alters aerosol chemistry and optical properties. EMIT-derived calcite improves agreement with airborne observations and reveals contrasts in dust alkalinity. Compared with globally averaged calcite, source-resolved calcite shifts regional annual mean aerosol pH by -0.6 to +0.5 units, with local changes exceeding 1 pH unit across substantial areas of the most affected dust-influenced regions, reaching -4 to +3 units in limited areas. These acidity changes reorganize secondary inorganic aerosol formation, nitrate partitioning, and extreme nitrate events, particularly where dust interacts with anthropogenic pollution. In contrast, calcite-driven secondary-aerosol radiative effects are small relative to those caused by spatial variations in iron-oxide absorption. These results show that calcite variability strongly modulates heterogeneous chemistry, whereas iron oxides dominate radiative impacts.

Abstract Given the large size of neurons, local maintenance of mitochondria is crucial to counteract insults to this organelle in axons and dendrites. The Parkinson-related mitochondrial kinase PINK1 plays a central role in mitochondrial quality control, which in neurons requires the transport of Pink1 mRNA by mitochondrial hitch-hiking. However, how and where PINK1 is locally translated and processed has remained unclear. Using live-cell imaging, we trace local PINK1 translation sites and preprotein dynamics, revealing a concerted interplay between mitochondria and the ER, with endolysosomes frequently localized adjacent to the site of translation. Upon metabolically regulated untethering from mitochondria, Pink1 mRNA relocates to ribosomes in proximity to the ER and endolysosomes for translation of the PINK1 preprotein. The ER chaperone DNAJB6 shields the PINK1 preprotein in transit to mitochondria, following the post-translational ER-SURF pathway. Consequently, loss of DNAJB6 leads to persistent ER/endolysosome-associated PINK1 precursor stores and failure of mitophagy upon mitochondrial damage. Our findings reveal that neuronal PINK1 protein translation switches between mitochondrially anchored co-translational and ER-associated post-translational import states, with functional implications for mitochondrial quality control.

item.title: A protein repeat interruption rule governs Nebulin stability and explains in-frame NEB mutations
item.description:
Lacramioara Fabian, Tasneem Y. Al Mudarris, Sylvia J. P. Bogaards, Senthuri Viththiyapaskaran, Esmat Karimi, Gerrie P. Farman, Xiucheng Cui, Jason Burgess, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79648-6
Abstract Nemaline myopathy is a rare congenital muscle disease associated with thin filament disruption that is currently without treatment. Biallelic mutations in Nebulin are the most common cause of nemaline myopathy. Nebulin encodes a giant protein with a primary function of establishing thin filament length. Nebulin protein has a large central region composed of a series of thin filament binding super repeats. Many Nebulin mutations are small in-frame deletions within individual super repeats. Why these deletions cause disease remains unclear. To study this, we generated a series of zebrafish lines, including ones carrying in-frame partial super repeat deletions and ones harboring complete/intact super repeat deletions. Partial super repeat deletions destabilize and reduce Nebulin protein, resulting in severe phenotypes and early death. Conversely, complete super repeat deletions preserve Nebulin stability and expression, and induce no overt phenotypes. Our work provides mechanistic insights and informs future therapeutic approaches for Nebulin-related Nemaline myopathy.
